h1: The 6 Best Toshiba Microwaves of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six Toshiba microwaves compared on capacity, wattage, inverter, smart sensor and air fry features to help you choose.
summary: The TOSHIBA ML-EM45PIT with inverter, smart sensor and 1.6 cu ft is our top Toshiba. The 1.6 cu ft Smart Sensor 1200W is the better-value large model, the flatbed inverter suits easy cleaning, the 1.2 cu ft Smart Sensor is the mid-size choice, the air fryer combo adds crisping, and the 0.9 cu ft is the compact pick.
intro: Toshiba sells many microwaves under near-identical names, and the biggest trap is assuming that two listings called Countertop Microwave Oven are the same machine. Capacity, wattage and whether there is a sensor or inverter decide what you actually get.

We reviewed eight Toshiba listings and ranked six distinct models on the spec sheet: capacity, wattage, smart sensor, inverter and air fry features, and price bucket. Where two listings looked identical we counted them once.

products.name: TOSHIBA ML-EM45PIT(SS) Countertop Microwave Oven with Inverter
products.verdict: Inverter, smart sensor and auto defrost in a 1.6 cu ft body.
products.description:
The ML-EM45PIT is a stainless steel Toshiba with inverter technology, a smart sensor and auto defrost, with 1.6 cu ft of capacity. It is priced $200-500.

Top spot comes from the combination of inverter, sensor and defrost, which no other Toshiba here lists together. The tradeoff against the cheaper 1.6 cu ft Smart Sensor model is the higher price bucket.

It suits cooks who want automatic settings and bigger dishes. The caveat is cost.
products.idealFor: Cooks wanting automatic settings and larger dishes.

products.name: TOSHIBA Microwave Oven with Smart Sensor
products.verdict: 1.6 cu ft, 1200W and a smart sensor for $100-200.
products.description:
This Toshiba lists a 1.6 cu ft interior, 1200W of power and a smart sensor, priced $100-200.

It ranks second because it matches the top pick on capacity and sensor for a lower price bucket, but it lacks the inverter and auto defrost listing. It is also the highest-wattage Toshiba alongside the flatbed.

It suits families wanting power and size without paying the top price. The caveat is no inverter.
products.idealFor: Families wanting power and space for less.

products.name: TOSHIBA Flatbed Microwave Oven with Inverter Technology
products.verdict: A flatbed 1.3 cu ft inverter model at 1200W.
products.description:
This flatbed Toshiba has inverter technology, 1.3 cu ft of capacity and 1200W, priced $100-200.

It places third because its interior is smaller than the 1.6 cu ft models, though it is the only flatbed and the cheapest with inverter. A flat floor means no turntable to clean.

It suits buyers who want inverter cooking at a lower bucket. The caveat is no sensor listed.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting inverter cooking for less.

products.name: TOSHIBA Countertop Microwave Oven with Smart Sensor
products.verdict: A 1.2 cu ft, 1000W model with a smart sensor.
products.description:
A smart sensor joins 1.2 cu ft of space and 1000W on this Toshiba, which is priced $100-200.

Fourth place reflects its smaller 1.2 cu ft cavity and lower wattage versus the 1.6 cu ft sensor model above. The sensor is what lifts it above a basic 1.2 cu ft Toshiba.

It suits couples who want a sensor at mid-size. The caveat is less power than the top models.
products.idealFor: Couples wanting a sensor at mid-size.

products.name: TOSHIBA Air Fryer Combo Microwave
products.verdict: A 1.0 cu ft microwave that also air fries.
products.description:
Toshiba's Air Fryer Combo is a 1.0 cu ft microwave that also air fries, priced $100-200.

It lands fifth because the cavity is small and the listing gives no wattage, yet it is the only Toshiba here that crisps food. That second function is its reason to exist.

It suits small kitchens that want one appliance. The caveat is limited space.

products.name: TOSHIBA Microwave Oven
products.description:
This is the smallest Toshiba here at 0.9 cu ft and 900W, priced $50-100.

It finishes last because capacity and power are the lowest of the six, but it is the cheapest by a bucket. You give up features for the lower price.

It suits dorms and offices. The caveat is no sensor or inverter listed.

whatMatters.detail: An inverter delivers steady power instead of cycling on and off, which can help food heat evenly. Two Toshibas here list it. Look for the word inverter in the title.
A sensor adjusts cooking by detecting steam, so you guess less. Several models list it. Check for smart sensor in the title or bullets.
Capacity here runs from 0.9 to 1.6 cu ft. Larger fits bigger dishes but needs counter space. Compare with your largest plate.
Higher watts heat faster. Models range from 900W to 1200W. Check the figure, since some listings omit it.
A flatbed removes the turntable and an air fry combo adds crisping. Decide whether you need either. Check the title for the feature name.

faq.a: The ML-EM45PIT and the 1200W Smart Sensor model both list 1.6 cu ft.
Assuming identically named Toshibas are the same. Wattage and sensors differ.

faq.q: Is the inverter worth the extra?
faq.a: If you want steady power and the full feature set, yes. The 1.6 cu ft Smart Sensor model costs less.

faq.q: How do I use smart sensor settings?
faq.a: Pick the sensor menu and let the microwave detect steam. Follow the manual.

faq.q: How do I clean a flatbed microwave?
faq.a: Wipe the flat floor with a damp cloth since there is no turntable to remove.

faq.q: Does the air fryer combo replace an air fryer?
faq.a: It adds air frying at 1.0 cu ft, so capacity is limited.

finalTake: The ML-EM45PIT is the best Toshiba for most buyers, with inverter, smart sensor and 1.6 cu ft. The 1.6 cu ft Smart Sensor model gives power for less, and the flatbed suits easy cleaning. Check wattage and sensor before ordering.
